title: The year the Sun went dim for 18 months ☁️
subject: sun
description:
Would you have survived 536? 👇

In 536 AD a mysterious fog dimmed the Sun across Europe, the Middle East and Asia for up to 18 months. Summers turned cold, snow fell in China in summer, and harvests failed from Ireland to China. Scientists think volcanic eruptions caused it; volcanic glass in Swiss Alpine ice points to Iceland, though the exact source is still studied.

Sources: Science (Gibbons, "Why 536 was 'the worst year to be alive'", 2018), Antiquity (Loveluck, McCormick et al., 2018), Live Science, AccuWeather

scenes.text: The Sun went dim for 18 months.
A writer said it shone like the Moon, without brightness.
It was the year 536. Across Europe, the Middle East and Asia, a strange fog hid the sky.
Summers turned cold, snow fell in China in summer, and harvests failed from Ireland to China.
But here's the strange part. Scientists found volcanic glass in Swiss Alpine ice, likely from an eruption in Iceland.
